related_questions.question: Should I get the COVID-19 vaccine after recovering from the infection?
related_questions.snippet: You should get an updated COVID-19 vaccine even if you already had COVID-19. Staying up to date with COVID-19 vaccines after you recover from COVID-19 infection provides added protection against the virus that causes COVID-19. Talk to your doctor if you have questions about getting a COVID-19 vaccine.
related_questions.title: Getting Your COVID-19 Vaccine - CDC

related_questions.question: Is there immunity to the previous COVID infection?

text_blocks.snippet: After recovering from a COVID-19 infection, natural immunity can offer protection against reinfection for several months, but this protection decreases over time. While reinfections can still occur, they are often milder, particularly if individuals are up-to-date on vaccinations and seek treatment promptly. However, immunity from prior infection may not be as robust against newer variants.
snippet_highlighted_words: natural immunity can offer protection against reinfection for several months, but this protection decreases over time

text_blocks.snippet: Key points about COVID-19 reinfection and immunity:

list.title: Reinfection is possible:
list.snippet: Individuals can be infected multiple times with the virus that causes COVID-19.

list.title: Protection decreases over time:
list.snippet: The immune response following infection wanes, making individuals susceptible to reinfection.

list.title: Severity can vary:
list.snippet: Reinfections can be mild, but severe illness is still possible, especially in those with weakened immune systems.

list.title: Vaccination is crucial:
list.snippet: Staying up-to-date with COVID-19 vaccinations can significantly reduce the risk of severe illness from reinfection.

list.title: Early treatment helps:
list.snippet: Seeking prompt treatment for COVID-19 can also help minimize the severity of the illness.

list.title: Omicron and beyond:
list.snippet: Research suggests that natural immunity after a COVID-19 infection has become less protective since the emergence of the Omicron variant.

related_questions.question: How long is immunity after a COVID vaccine?

text_blocks.snippet: COVID-19 vaccine-induced immunity can last for around six months, but this can vary. To maintain optimal protection, updated COVID-19 vaccines are recommended. The 2024-25 COVID-19 vaccine, for example, is designed to offer better protection against currently circulating variants. Most people need only one dose of the updated vaccine, though some individuals like those who are immunocompromised or between 6 months and 4 years old may need more.
